title: Probability: Outcomes of Simple Experiments
seo_title: Grade 4 Probability Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Perform simple repeated events and list possible outcomes for experiments such as tossing a coin or rolling a die; count and compare the frequency of actual outcomes for a series of trials.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 4 probability worksheets: possible outcomes of coins, dice and spinners, likelihood words and repeated experiments. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Outcomes are all the possible results.
key_sub: Each face of a fair die is equally likely.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • An outcome is a possible result. Tossing a coin has 2 outcomes: heads or tails. Rolling a die has 6: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.
  • Describe how likely an event is: impossible, unlikely, even chance, likely, certain.
  • Do an experiment many times and count the results in a tally table.
  • Results change from one experiment to the next, but more trials give a better picture.

Examples

Example

Toss a coin 20 times: 11 heads

20 − 11

Answer: 9 tails

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Missing outcomesList them all in order.
6 is harder to rollEach number on a fair die is equally likely.
Same results every timeChance gives different results.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 4 say about probability?
faq.a: Perform simple repeated events and list possible outcomes, such as tossing a coin or rolling a die, and count and compare the frequency of actual outcomes.
A possible result of an experiment.

faq.q: Is getting heads more likely after many tails?
faq.a: No. Each toss is a new chance.
More trials show the pattern better.

items.q: Kabelo tosses a coin. Which list shows all the possible outcomes?
items.e: A coin can land on heads or on tails. List each outcome once: heads, tails.

items.q: Refilwe rolls a dice. Which list shows all the possible outcomes?
items.e: A dice has 6 faces with 1 to 6 dots. Any face can land on top. There is no 0.

items.q: This spinner has 6 sections. How many different outcomes (colours) are there?
items.e: Count the different colours, not the sections: red, blue and yellow. That is 3 outcomes.

items.q: Precious picks one counter without looking. Which list shows all the possible outcomes?
items.e: The counter can be red or green. Green is possible, even though there are fewer green counters. There is no blue.

items.q: Number cards 1 to 8 are face down. Liam picks one card. How many possible outcomes are there?
items.e: Any card from 1 to 8 can be picked: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. That is 8 outcomes.

items.q: Sibusiso spins this spinner. Which outcome is impossible?
items.e: The spinner has the numbers 1 to 5. There is no 6, so landing on 6 is impossible.

items.q: Rolling a number from 1 to 6 on a dice is …
items.e: Every roll gives 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6. It must happen, so it is certain.

items.q: Picking a yellow counter from this bag is …
items.e: The bag has only blue and green counters. There is no yellow, so it is impossible.

items.q: Landing on purple is …
items.e: Purple is only a quarter of the spinner. It can happen, but not often, so it is unlikely.

items.q: Rolling a number greater than 2 on a dice is …
items.e: Greater than 2: 3, 4, 5, 6. That is 4 of the 6 faces, so it is likely. It is not certain, because 1 or 2 could come up.

items.q: Thandi tosses a coin. What are the possible outcomes?
items.e: A coin has two sides: heads and tails. It can land on either one, so the outcomes are heads or tails.

items.q: Kabelo rolls a dice. What are all the possible outcomes?
items.e: A dice has 6 faces with 1 to 6 dots. Any face can land on top: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6. There is no 0.

items.q: How many different outcomes are there when you roll a dice?
items.e: The outcomes are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6. That is 6 outcomes.

items.q: Which number is impossible to roll on a dice?
items.e: A dice shows 1 to 6. There is no 7, so rolling a 7 is impossible.

items.q: Rolling a number less than 7 on a dice is …
items.e: Every number on a dice (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6) is less than 7. It must happen, so it is certain.

items.q: Rolling a number greater than 6 on a dice is …
items.e: The biggest number on a dice is 6. You can never roll more than 6, so it is impossible.

items.q: Rolling a 6 on a dice is …
items.e: Only 1 of the 6 faces shows 6. It can happen, but it is unlikely.

items.q: Rolling a number greater than 1 on a dice is …
items.e: 5 of the 6 faces are greater than 1 (2, 3, 4, 5, 6). Only the 1 is not. So it is likely.

items.q: Dumisani thinks a 6 is harder to roll than a 1, because 6 is a bigger number. Is he right?
items.e: Each face of a dice has the same chance. The size of the number does not matter. 1 and 6 are each 1 face out of 6, so they are equally likely.

items.q: Refilwe tosses a coin. Getting heads is …
items.e: A coin has one heads side and one tails side, so heads and tails are equally likely.

items.q: The month after March will be April. This is …
items.e: The months always come in the same order. April always comes after March, so it is certain.

items.q: Next year will have 13 months. This is …
items.e: Every year has 12 months. A year can never have 13 months, so it is impossible.

items.q: A tortoise will walk across the school playground today. This is …
items.e: Tortoises live in the veld and hardly ever come into a school. It is not impossible, but it almost never happens, so it is unlikely.

items.q: If today is Saturday, tomorrow will be Sunday. This is …
items.e: Sunday always comes after Saturday, so it is certain.

items.q: Thabo will grow 2 metres taller this week. This is …
items.e: Children grow a few centimetres a year, not 2 metres in a week. It can never happen, so it is impossible.

items.q: A kookaburra will land on Ofentse’s desk during maths. This is …
items.e: A kookaburra could fly into a classroom, but it hardly ever happens. So it is unlikely, not impossible.

items.q: Thandi throws a ball up into the air. It will come back down. This is …
items.e: A ball thrown up always falls back down. It must happen, so it is certain.

items.q: Tebogo buys 1 ticket in a raffle. 200 tickets are sold. Tebogo will win. This is …
items.e: Tebogo has only 1 of the 200 tickets. He could win, but it is unlikely.

items.q: A goldfish will climb a tree. This is …
items.e: A goldfish lives in water and cannot climb. It can never happen, so it is impossible.

items.q: Dark clouds cover the sky. Pieter says, “It is certain to rain today.” Which word is better?
items.e: Dark clouds mean rain will probably come, but the clouds might blow away. It could still not rain, so it is likely, not certain.

items.q: The sun will rise tomorrow morning. This is …
items.e: The sun rises every morning. It always happens, so it is certain.

items.q: After Wednesday, the next day will be Thursday. This is …
items.e: The days of the week always come in the same order. Thursday always comes after Wednesday, so it is certain.

items.q: A zebra will fly over the school like a bird. This is …
items.e: Zebras run, but they cannot fly. This can never happen, so it is impossible.

items.q: Kabelo is 8. Next year he will be 9. This is …
items.e: Everyone is one year older each year. 8 + 1 = 9, so it is certain.

items.q: Tomorrow will have 30 hours. This is …
items.e: Every day has 24 hours. A day can never have 30 hours, so it is impossible.

items.q: A lion will walk into the classroom today. This is …
items.e: Lions live in trees in the bush. One could wander into a school, but it hardly ever happens. So it is unlikely, not impossible.

items.q: If Thandi drops a tennis ball, it will fall down. This is …
items.e: When you let go of a ball, it always falls to the ground. It must happen, so it is certain.

items.q: Sibusiso is 8. Next year he will be 3 years old. This is …
items.e: You cannot get younger. Next year Sibusiso will be 9, so being 3 is impossible.

items.q: The next vehicle that drives past the school will have 4 wheels. This is …
items.e: Most vehicles on the road are cars with 4 wheels. But the next one could be a motorbike or a truck, so it is likely, not certain.

items.q: Precious will drink some water at school today. This is …
items.e: Most learners drink water during a school day. Precious could forget, so it is likely, not certain.

items.q: The spinner has 4 equal sections. Which colour is the arrow most likely to land on?
c: red and blue are equally likely
items.e: 3 of the 4 equal sections are red and only 1 is blue, so red is most likely. (There is no green, so green is impossible.)

items.q: The spinner has 6 equal sections. Which colour is the arrow least likely to land on?
items.e: Only 1 of the 6 equal sections is green. 5 are yellow. Green has the smallest part, so it is least likely.

items.q: Landing on red is …
items.e: Every section is red. The arrow must land on red, so it is certain.

items.q: Landing on red is …
items.e: Only 1 of the 6 equal sections is red. It can happen, but not often, so it is unlikely. It is not impossible, because there is a red section.

items.q: Landing on green is …
items.e: There is no green section on this spinner. The arrow can never land on green, so it is impossible.

items.q: Landing on green is …
items.e: 5 of the 6 equal sections are green, so green is likely. It is not certain, because there is 1 purple section.

items.q: Which colour can the arrow never land on?
items.e: The spinner has red, blue and yellow sections only. There is no green, so landing on green is impossible.

items.q: Which colour is the arrow most likely to land on?
c: all three colours are equally likely
items.e: Look at the size of each part, not the number of sections. Blue is one big section: half of the spinner. Red is 2 small sections (a quarter) and yellow is 2 small sections (a quarter). So blue is most likely.

items.q: Which two colours are equally likely?
items.e: Red and green are each a quarter of the spinner. Parts of the same size are equally likely. Yellow is half of the spinner, so it is more likely than red or green.

items.q: Landing on yellow is …
items.e: Yellow is only a quarter of the spinner and green is three quarters. Yellow can happen, but it is unlikely.

items.q: Palesa picks one counter from the bag without looking. Which colour is she most likely to pick?
c: red and blue are equally likely
items.e: There are 6 red counters and only 2 blue counters. More red counters means red is more likely.

items.q: Dumisani picks one counter without looking. Which colour is he least likely to pick?
items.e: There is only 1 green counter and 7 yellow counters, so green is least likely.

items.q: Picking a blue counter from this bag is …
items.e: Every counter in the bag is blue, so you must pick blue. It is certain.

items.q: Picking a green counter from this bag is …
items.e: There are only red and yellow counters. There is no green counter, so it is impossible.

items.q: Picking a red counter from this bag is …
items.e: 7 of the 8 counters are red, so red is likely. It is not certain, because there is 1 blue counter.

items.q: Picking a red counter from this bag is …
items.e: Only 1 of the 10 counters is red. It can happen, but not often, so it is unlikely, not impossible.

items.q: Which colour is impossible to pick from this bag?
items.e: The bag has red, blue and yellow counters. There is no green, so green is impossible. There is 1 yellow counter, so yellow is unlikely, not impossible.

items.q: Which sentence is true?
c: Red is more likely than blue
Red and blue are equally likely
items.e: There are 4 red and 4 blue counters. The same number of each colour means they are equally likely.

items.q: This bag has 9 green marbles and 1 purple marble. Sarah picks one marble without looking. Picking the purple marble is …
items.e: Only 1 of the 10 marbles is purple. It can happen, but it is unlikely.

items.q: Which two colours are equally likely to be picked?
items.e: There are 3 red, 3 blue and 2 yellow counters. Red and blue have the same number, so they are equally likely.

items.q: Which colour came up most often?
c: They all came up the same
items.e: Red: 2 groups of 5 and 4 more = 14. Blue: 10. Yellow: 6. Red has the most tally marks.

items.q: How many times did Ofentse spin altogether?
items.e: Add the tallies: 14 + 10 + 6 = 30.

items.q: How many more times did red come up than yellow?
items.e: Red 14, yellow 6. How many more means subtract: 14 − 6 = 8.

items.q: Ofentse’s spinner has 6 equal sections. Which spinner did she most likely use?
items.e: Red came up most, then blue, then yellow, so red should have the most sections and yellow the fewest. It cannot have 0 yellow, because yellow came up 6 times.

items.q: Which number did Thabo roll most often?
items.e: The biggest number in the Times row is 12, under the number 5. (6 is the biggest number on the dice, not the one rolled most.)

items.q: Thabo says 5 is the easiest number to roll, because it came up most. Is he right?
c: Yes, 5 will come up most every time
No, 3 is the easiest to roll
No, 6 is the easiest to roll
No, each number is equally likely
items.e: Each face of a dice has the same chance. Results vary: next time a different number may come up most.

items.q: How many times did Thabo roll an even number?
items.e: Even numbers: 2, 4 and 6. Add their results: 11 + 10 + 10 = 31. (29 is the odd numbers.)

items.q: Refilwe tosses a coin 20 times and gets 12 heads and 8 tails. She tosses it 20 more times. What will happen?
c: The results will probably be a little different
She will get 12 tails and 8 heads
items.e: Chance results vary each time. She might get 9 heads, or 11, or 12. We cannot know for sure.

items.q: Pieter spins this spinner 40 times. Which result would be most surprising?
items.e: Half the spinner is red and half is blue, so you expect about 20 of each. Results near 20 are normal. Red every single time is possible, but very unlikely.

items.q: Tebogo spins this spinner 40 times. Which result is most likely?
items.e: Blue is three quarters of the spinner, so blue should come up about 3 times as often as red. Blue 30 and red 10 fits best.

items.q: For 10 spins, Lerato predicted 5 red. How far from the prediction was her result?
items.e: She got 8 red. 8 − 5 = 3. (6 is the difference between red and blue.)

items.q: In the 100 spins, how many more times did red come up than blue?
items.e: Red 54, blue 46. How many more means subtract: 54 − 46 = 8.

items.q: Which number of spins gave a result closest to half red?
items.e: Half of 10 is 5 (she got 8). Half of 100 is 50 (she got 54). Half of 1 000 is 500 (she got 508). 508 out of 1 000 is closest to half.

items.q: What usually happens when you do more trials of an experiment?
c: Results get closer to the prediction
Results get further from the prediction
items.e: With only a few trials, results can be far off. With many trials, the results usually come close to the prediction, but not always exactly.

items.q: Lungile wants to test whether a spinner is fair. Which plan is best?
items.e: More trials give results closer to the true chances. 200 spins tells you much more than 2 or 10.

items.q: Sibusiso tosses a coin 10 times and gets 7 heads. What can he say?
c: 10 tosses is too few to tell
items.e: With only 10 tosses, 7 heads happens quite often with a fair coin. He needs many more tosses to tell.

items.q: Mr. Gill’s class has 5 groups. Each group spins a spinner with 1 red and 3 blue equal sections 20 times. How many spins did the class do altogether?
items.e: 5 groups × 20 spins = 100 spins.

items.q: Mr. Gill’s class has 5 groups. Each group spins a spinner with 1 red and 3 blue equal sections 20 times. How many times did red come up altogether?
items.e: Add the groups: 4 + 7 + 5 + 3 + 6 = 25. (75 is the number of blues: 100 − 25.)

items.q: Mr. Gill’s class has 5 groups. Each group spins a spinner with 1 red and 3 blue equal sections 20 times. Each group predicted 5 reds. Which group’s result matched the prediction?
items.e: Look for 5 in the Red row. It is under group 3.

items.q: Mr. Gill’s class has 5 groups. Each group spins a spinner with 1 red and 3 blue equal sections 20 times. For 100 spins, the class predicted 25 reds. Which result was closest to its prediction?
items.e: Group 2 got 7 (2 away from 5). Group 4 got 3 (2 away). Group 5 got 6 (1 away). The whole class got 25: exactly the prediction. More trials gave a closer result.

items.q: Dumisani will spin this spinner 20 times. About how many times should he predict red?
items.e: Red is 1 of 4 equal sections, so about 1 spin in every 4 is red. 20 ÷ 4 = 5. 15 is the prediction for blue.

items.q: Dumisani will spin this spinner 20 times. About how many times should he predict blue?
items.e: Blue is 3 of 4 equal sections. 20 ÷ 4 = 5, and 3 × 5 = 15.

items.q: How many times did the arrow land on red?
items.e: Count the tally marks for red: 1 group of 5 and 2 more. 5 + 2 = 7.

items.q: Dumisani predicted red about 5 times. How many more times did red come up than he predicted?
items.e: Red came up 7 times. 7 − 5 = 2 more than predicted.

items.q: Red came up 7 times, not 5. What does this show?
c: Red is now more likely than blue
Red should come up exactly 5 times
Results are often a little different from a prediction
items.e: A prediction says about how many. Real results vary a little each time. 7 is close to 5, so nothing is wrong with the spinner.

items.q: Pieter will toss a coin 40 times. Which prediction is best?
items.e: Heads and tails are equally likely, so predict heads about half of the time. Half of 40 is 20.

items.q: Pieter predicted 20 heads. How far from the prediction was his result?
items.e: Heads came up 23 times. 23 − 20 = 3. (6 is the difference between heads and tails.)

items.q: Lungile rolled a number cube 30 times. Each number is equally likely. About how many times should she have predicted each number?
items.e: The cube has 6 equally likely faces. 30 ÷ 6 = 5 times each.

items.q: Which number came up most often?
items.e: Find the biggest number in the Times row: 7. It is under the number 4. (7 is how many times, and 6 is just the biggest number on the cube.)

items.q: Which number came up the fewest times?
items.e: Find the smallest number in the Times row: 3. It is under the number 5. (3 is how many times, not the number on the cube.)

items.q: Which colour came up most often?
c: they all came up the same
items.e: Red: 1 group of 5 and 4 more = 9. Blue: 7. Yellow: 4. Red has the most tally marks.

items.q: How many times did Ofentse spin altogether?
items.e: Add the tallies: 9 + 7 + 4 = 20.

items.q: How many more times did red come up than yellow?
items.e: Red 9, yellow 4. How many more means subtract: 9 − 4 = 5.

items.q: Pieter spins this spinner 20 times. Which result would be most surprising?
items.e: Half the spinner is red and half is blue, so you expect about 10 of each. Results near 10 are normal. Red every single time is possible, but very unlikely.

items.q: Tebogo spins this spinner 20 times. Which result is most likely?
items.e: 3 of the 4 equal sections are blue, so blue should come up about 3 times as often as red. Blue 15 and red 5 fits best. The results can change a little each time.

items.q: Refilwe tosses a coin 10 times and gets 6 heads and 4 tails. She tosses it 10 more times. What will happen?
c: She will get 6 tails and 4 heads
The results may be different this time
items.e: Chance results change each time. She might get 6 heads again, or 5, or 3. We cannot know for sure.

items.q: Which number did Kabelo roll most often?
items.e: Find the biggest number in the Times row: 7. That is under the number 5. (6 is the biggest number on the dice, not the most rolled.)

items.q: Kabelo says 5 is the easiest number to roll, because it came up most. Is he right?
c: No, each number is equally likely
No, 4 is the easiest to roll
No, 6 is the easiest to roll
Yes, 5 will come up most every time
items.e: Each face of a dice has the same chance. Results vary: next time a different number may come up most.

items.q: Thabo picks a counter from a bag, looks at it and puts it back. He does this 20 times. He gets red 17 times and blue 3 times. Which bag did he most likely use?
items.e: Red came up much more often than blue, so the bag probably has many more red counters. It cannot be 10 red and 0 blue, because then blue would be impossible, and he picked blue 3 times.

items.q: Lerato’s spinner has 4 equal sections. Which spinner did she most likely use?
items.e: Green came up 14 times and purple 6 times. Green came up much more often, so green probably covers more of the spinner. With 4 purple sections, green would be impossible.
